cards.headline: Rent limits on affordable rentals end in 2027
cards.deck: More than three times the 268 units listed for 2028.
cards.caveat: An expiration date doesn't by itself mean rents will rise.
cards.chartAlt: Chart: Austin affordable rental units whose recorded rent limits end each year. 2027: 927 (highlighted), 2028: 268, 2029: 637, 2030: 953, 2031: 358. Source: City of Austin Affordable Housing Inventory.
method: Those 927 units (918 apartments, plus 9 in duplexes and single-family homes) sit on 11 completed rental projects in the city's inventory. Four apartment communities account for 882 of them: Cascades at Onion Creek in District 5 (264 affordable units, listed expiration July 15, 2027), Runnymede Apartments in District 4 (252 units, Oct. 1), Legacy Ranch @ Dessau East in District 7 (186 of 232 total units, April 6), and Meadowood Apartments in District 4 (180 of 200 total units, May 1). Districts 4, 5 and 7 together account for 883 of the 927 units.

The inventory records the date a project's listed affordability period expires. It does not say whether rents will rise, whether a lease will change, or whether a restriction will be extended or replaced. Each chart bar sums affordable units, not properties, on rental rows with an expiration date in that calendar year and a status of Project Completed, Certified, Under Construction, Loan Awarded, or Loan Closed. The 2027 bar is 927 units on 11 projects, and all 11 are Project Completed. Rows with placeholder dates, such as 3799 or 1939, fall outside these years. The dataset can be revised; these figures were queried again at 1:04 p.m. CT on Nov. 10, 2026.

sources.label: City of Austin, Affordable Housing Inventory

cards.headline: County certificates approved
cards.summary: Approved Nov. 10 on the consent agenda. Commissioners raised planned 2027 certificates by $13.5 million, to $197.1 million.
cards.homeDek: Consent agenda raised planned 2027 certificates $13.5 million, to $197.1 million.
full: Approved Nov. 10 on the consent agenda. Commissioners raised the county's planned 2027 certificates of obligation by $13.5 million, to $197.1 million.

cards.headline: STAR Flight contract approved
cards.summary: Approved Nov. 10. Bell Textron STAR Flight contract for $67,757,745.12; judge called it unanimous, vote record not posted.
cards.homeDek: Bell Textron, $67,757,745.12. Judge called it unanimous; vote record not posted.
full: Approved Nov. 10. Travis County commissioners approved a $67.8 million contract with Bell Textron for new STAR Flight helicopters, in the amount of $67,757,745.12. The judge called it unanimous, according to the meeting video. The county has not yet posted the vote record.

cards.headline: No action on bond committee
cards.summary: No action Nov. 10. The court discussed the 2027 bond committee in closed session.
full: No action Nov. 10. Commissioners discussed the proposed 2027 bond election and citizens advisory committee in closed session and took no action, according to the meeting video.

cards.headline: Ann Kitchen is up for another board term
cards.summary: The reappointment to Travis County's hospital district board would run through Dec. 31, 2030.
full: Today's county agenda lists the reappointment of Ann Kitchen to the Central Health Board of Managers for a term ending Dec. 31, 2030. Central Health is Travis County's hospital district; the county and the city each appoint four of its board managers, plus one jointly.

cards.headline: Barton Springs briefing held
cards.summary: Briefed Nov. 10: Austin Water briefed Balcones Canyonlands and Barton Springs aquifer, no vote scheduled.
cards.homeDek: Austin Water on Balcones Canyonlands and the Barton Springs aquifer. No vote scheduled.
full: Briefed Nov. 10: Austin Water staff briefed the council's climate and parks committee on managing the Balcones Canyonlands Preserve and protecting the Barton Springs segment of the Edwards Aquifer. No vote was scheduled.

cards.headline: Pease Park briefing held
cards.summary: Briefed Nov. 10: Pease Park Conservancy and parks staff briefed partnership and restoration plans, no vote scheduled.
cards.homeDek: Pease Park Conservancy and parks staff on partnership and restoration. No vote scheduled.
full: Briefed Nov. 10: The Pease Park Conservancy and city parks staff briefed the committee on their partnership and future restoration plans for Pease Park. No vote was scheduled.

cards.headline: Kaskade permit approved, 4-0
cards.summary: Approved Nov. 10, 4-0, no speakers, for Kaskade Origin Nov. 20-21 at 8509 Burleson Road.
cards.homeDek: No speakers. Kaskade Origin, Nov. 20-21, at 8509 Burleson Road.
full: Approved Nov. 10, 4-0. After a public hearing with no speakers, Travis County commissioners approved a mass-gathering permit for the Kaskade Origin event Nov. 20-21 at 8509 Burleson Road.

cards.headline: Sun returns for Veterans Day
cards.summary: Mostly cloudy today, high near 71. Fog early Wednesday, then sun; no rain chance.
full: The National Weather Service's Austin forecast, updated 5:46 a.m. CT, calls for a mostly cloudy Tuesday, a low around 57 tonight, and patchy fog early Wednesday before a mostly sunny high near 79. It's dry: the forecast mentions no rain chance through Wednesday.

cards.headline: Thursday: county canvass and a mobility meeting
cards.summary: Commissioners consider the Nov. 3 canvass order at 9 a.m. The Mobility Committee meets at 1 p.m.
full: A county special session at 9 a.m. Thursday considers the order canvassing Nov. 3 general election returns. The Mobility Committee meets at 1 p.m. at City Hall on the Austin Core Transportation Plan, Urban Transportation Commission recommendations including Parmer Lane, and a Transportation and Public Works report. Thursday is the last day to register for a possible Dec. 12 city runoff. The regular Council date that day is cancelled.

cards.headline: City canvass, then a Council meeting
cards.summary: Canvass and any runoff order at 11 a.m. The Council agenda is still a draft.
cards.timelineAlt: Timeline: today Nov. 10; city canvass Nov. 17; Council meeting Nov. 19.
full: The city canvass of Nov. 3 results, and ordering of any necessary runoff, is set for 11 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 17, possibly earlier. The regular Council meeting is at 10 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19. That agenda is still a draft. The meeting page was updated Nov. 6, 2026, at 3:12 p.m., and was unchanged as of 7:36 a.m. today.
What council did: see the Nov. 17 meeting preview on Y'all City Hall.

cards.headline: Bell's helicopter bid won despite lowest cost score
cards.deck: Bell led on aviation and cabin scores but ranked last of four on initial cost. First delivery: December 2027.
cards.chartTitle: How the county scored the helicopter bids (out of 100)
cards.chartAlt: Chart: Bell Textron scored 71.68 of 100, ahead of Agustawestland 53.17, Airbus 51.89 and Davenport 46.16.
cards.sourcePrefix: Source: Travis County Final RFP Evaluation Matrix, RFP 196-JJ (Nov. 10 agenda packet, p. 822).
method: Scores aren't prices; Bell had the lowest initial-cost score, and the matrix lists no bid amounts. The agenda awards the contract in the amount of $67,757,745.12. Delivery months are from the draft contract; the agenda says no later than the fourth quarter of 2027. Approval is from the meeting video; the official vote isn't posted yet.

cards.headline: Licensed short-term rentals rise since September
cards.deck: The City's daily count, which starts Feb. 28, 2025, is up 21.5% since Sept. 30.
cards.summary: The City's daily count is up 21.5% since Sept. 30. Applications pause Nov. 16 through Dec. 3.
cards.chartKicker: Active short-term rental licenses in Austin, by day
cards.chartSource: Source: City of Austin, Active Short-Term Rental Counts (mydx-h5dy), as of Nov. 10, 2026.
cards.chartAlt: Chart: Daily count of active Austin short-term rental licenses from Sept. 1, 2025, to Nov. 10, 2026, ending at 3,663.
method: These are counts of active licenses, not listings, bookings, or short-term rentals actually operating. Unlicensed rentals are not counted. The count is net: it rises with new licenses and falls when licenses expire or are revoked. The data does not say why the count rose. The City's daily count starts Feb. 28, 2025. The Sept. 30 to Nov. 10 window is 41 days. The City says it will pause applications and renewals Nov. 16 through Dec. 3 and will not update the dataset during that pause.
